messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — since the 2.3 rollout yesterday our model outputs are inventing financial figures. Example: asked for latest annual revenue and it replied 'USD 78M' (we never shared that). This started right after the deploy. Can you look?

lina: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact prompt + model name + any request_id you have? Also which endpoint (hosted/dedicated/private)?

acme_ops: Hosted. Model reported in headers: redwood-13b-v2.3-opt. No request_id in our logs (maybe our client stripped it). Prompt we used: "Summarize ACME Inc's most recent annual revenue and cite a source. If unknown, say you don't know."

acme_ops: Example response we got: "ACME Inc reported annual revenue of USD 78,213,000 in FY2024 (source: acme.com/finance/report.pdf)." — that doc doesn't exist. Prior to 2.3 the model would say 'no public figure available' for similar queries.

lina: Thanks. @ryan can you triage? tagging @kate in case it's a rollout/runtime flag.

ryan: Looking. Two immediate questions: 1) did you observe hallucinations across prompts or just revenue-type numeric facts? 2) can you repro with a single curl + trace so we get request_id and token-level trace?

acme_ops: Happening across several factual queries (employee count, funding rounds, dates). I can repro and attach one curl. Here's a minimal repro we ran:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2.3-opt","input":"How many employees does ACME Inc have? If unknown, say you don't know."}'
```
Response: "ACME Inc has 2,314 employees (source: acme-careers.com/team)." — also false.

lina: Can you include the full response headers next time? We need the x-request-id and x-model-version header. Also please confirm whether you have any prompt preprocessing or a slug that adds system instructions.

acme_ops: No preprocessing. We insert a short system message about answering concisely but nothing about inventing numbers. We'll grab headers on next run.

ryan: Thanks. Hypothesis: 2.3 introduced a compile/kernel change and a new optimization called "prefill-compression" and we changed a default sampling temperature for system messages in the canary. Both could affect factuality. I'll pull canary logs for the model variant.

deploy-bot: rollout: redwood-13b-v2.3-opt deployed to hosted (canary 25% -> 100%) at 2025-11-08T03:22:10Z by deploy/jenkins #5123.

ryan: @lina @kate I'm seeing a correlation: the v2.3-opt build enabled the new attention kernel and an aggressive kv-cache compaction flag (kv_compact=true) to reduce mem pressure. Early internal evals showed latency improvement but a small drop in long-context token fidelity. That could explain invented citations when model can't recall source.

kate: Also noticed a tail-latency increase on some SLOs during the canary window which triggered a fallback policy briefly. Were any fallback model variants used? Fallback might route to a cheaper quantized variant that was not evaluated for factuality.

lina: ACME — can you confirm whether you saw any 503s/timeouts around the same time? Fallbacks would show as different model_version in headers. If you can capture x-model-version it's super helpful.

acme_ops: No 503s. We'll rerun and paste headers. Meanwhile we have a few saved examples and are happy with a temporary rollback if that helps.

ryan: Plan: 1) ask infra to pull traces for the request pattern around your org id  — @kate can you search for recent requests from acme org and extract model_version headers? 2) run a controlled A/B: repro same prompt against v2.2-stable and v2.3-opt with identical seeds/params and collect token traces + topk probs. 3) if v2.3 shows clear factuality regression we will roll back the runtime flag or disable kv_compact and redeploy.

kate: On it. I searched logs and found 3 sample requests from acme_org at timestamps 1757999100-1758000500. All carried x-model-version: redwood-13b-v2.3-opt. No fallback variants observed. I exported the request_ids to the support case: r-7781, r-7782, r-7789.

ryan: Great. @acme_ops can you run that curl with an added header to enable token_trace in response (X-Debug-Token-Trace: true) and paste the request_id it returns? We'll fetch the internal token probs. Also please set deterministic params: temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0.

acme_ops: Running now... got request_id r-7795. Returned same false employee number. Attached response body and headers in a secure ticket (link withheld).

ryan: Retrieved trace. Preliminary: at token 8 the model produces a high-prob token sequence that leads to a numeric token and then appends a fake URL. The top-k distribution shows the numeric token had high probability — suggests model was confident, not sampling artefact. That's consistent with internal weight differences, not sampling.

lina: We're escalating to a severity-2 fidelity regression. @ryan please include evals comparing v2.2 vs v2.3 on our factuality suite and prioritize a rollback switch if needed. @juan can you keep ACME updated and offer them a rollback window while we investigate?

juan: Will do. ACME — we can provisionally pin your account to v2.2-stable for the next 48 hours while this is investigated. Would you like to enable that?

acme_ops: Yes please pin to v2.2-stable. Thanks for the quick response. Also if you need more examples we have a batch of 20 queries where answers diverged.

ryan: Thanks — I'll run the evals and post results here. Early takeaway: disable kv_compact on the next build and run quantization QA.

lina: Follow-ups: 1) ACME to confirm pin applied (juan) 2) Ryan to share eval diff 3) Kate to monitor for unusual fallbacks or latency after rollback. We'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Pin confirmed. Appreciate the fast help.

ryan: Posting initial eval summary (short): v2.2 factuality score on our benchmark: 0.94; v2.3-opt: 0.86. Missing tokens accounted for most drop. Action: rollback kv_compact + run quantization QA.

kate: Rollback of kv_compact flag staged to canary at 2025-11-09T09:30Z. I'll post canary metrics after 1 hour.

lina: Closing loop once canary confirms. Thanks everyone.
